agents.description:
AI agents and automation using agent tokens (AGT-004, AGT-009). Shared across a
cluster, so `enabled = false` switches every agent off everywhere.

api.description: The REST API (and, later, the web UI).

auth.description: Sign-in: sessions, HTTP Basic, two-factor policy (API-003).

client.description: Known devices and how to recognize them (FLT-006).

cluster.description: Cluster identity (full cluster settings arrive with M5).

group.description: Client groups (FLT-005). A `default` group (every list) exists even if not declared.

list.description: Filter lists: blocklists and allowlists from URLs, files, or inline rules (`spec/05`).

listen.description: DNS listeners. Setting `[[listen]]` replaces the defaults entirely.

local.description: Local data settings (hosts files, PTR generation).

node.description: This node's role and local settings.

route.description: Per-domain / per-group / per-qtype routing to upstream groups.

rule.description:
Quick rules (T6.12, ADR-067): allow or block a domain for some devices, some groups,
or everyone, optionally until a time. They decide before any list.

updates.description: Whether to check for newer builds (OPS-004, ADR-046).

upstream_group.description: Named groups of upstreams with a selection strategy.

AccessConfig.description: Who may use this resolver (`spec/08` §6: never an open resolver by default).

allowed_networks.description:
Clients outside these networks get REFUSED. Default: private (RFC 1918), CGNAT /
Tailscale (100.64/10), ULA, link-local, and loopback.

items.description: IP network, e.g. "192.168.0.0/16" or "fd00::/8" (a bare address means a single host).

enabled.description:
The kill switch: `false` refuses every agent token at once (users and their own
tokens are unaffected).

rate_per_minute.description: Requests per minute per agent token, unless the token sets its own.

require_approval.description:
REQ: AGT-007 — agents' planned changes wait for an operator's approval ("Agent
changes" in the web UI) before `apply_plan` succeeds.

AnomalyConfig.description:
Device anomaly detection (OBS-013, ADR-019): rate spikes, heavy volume to one domain,
drift to many new domains, and regular phone-home beacons, each against the device's own
learned baseline. Findings never block anything.

ignore_domains.description: Registrable domains never reported (e.g. connectivity checks you expect).

learning_days.description: Days a device is watched before it can raise a finding.

max_clients.description: Devices with state; the least recently seen are evicted first.

AnomalySensitivity.description: How readily the anomaly engine reports (`spec/06` §7.1).

oneOf.description: Only large departures from a device's baseline.
Smaller departures too (more findings, more false alarms).

ApiConfig.description:
REST API listener (API-001). It also serves `/metrics` (signed in) and the health probes,
only to clients in `[access] allowed_networks` (ADR-029).

trusted_proxies.description:
Reverse proxies or ingress controllers in front of the API (e.g. the pod network,
`10.0.0.0/8`). For requests from them, the client address comes from
`X-Forwarded-For` (sign-in lockouts, break-glass networks, the audit log). Default:
none (the connection's address is the client).

items.description: IP network, e.g. "192.168.0.0/16" or "fd00::/8" (a bare address means a single host).

AuthConfig.description:
Sign-in settings (API-003, `spec/08` §6). Users, sessions, and tokens live in
`<data_dir>/state.db`. The first admin comes from the one-time setup token (in the log
and `<data_dir>/setup-token`) or from `TELLTALE_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USER` with
`TELLTALE_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` or `TELLTALE_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH`.

allow_insecure_basic.description:
Accept HTTP Basic over plain HTTP. Off: Basic only behind HTTPS (a proxy that sends
`X-Forwarded-Proto: https`).

oidc.description: Sign-in through `OpenID Connect` providers (Keycloak, Authentik, ...; API-004).

session_ttl_hours.description: A UI session ends this long after sign-in (default 168 = 7 days).

totp_required_roles.description: Roles that must use two-factor sign-in (TOTP), e.g. `["admin"]`.

oneOf.description: A → 0.0.0.0, AAAA → ::, anything else → NODATA (Pi-hole and Technitium default).
A/AAAA → `block_ips` (e.g. a "blocked" landing page); other types → NODATA.

max_entries.description: Optional cap on entry count (0 = limited by bytes only).

persist.description: Dump the cache on shutdown and reload it on start (DNS-009).

prefetch.description: Refresh hot entries before they expire (DNS-008).

prefetch_min_hits.description: Minimum hits before an entry is prefetched.

prefetch_threshold_pct.description: Prefetch when remaining TTL drops below this percentage.

serve_stale.description: Serve expired answers when upstreams fail (RFC 8767, DNS-007).

servfail_ttl.description: How long SERVFAIL is cached, seconds (RFC 9520).

stale_answer_client_timeout_ms.description: Answer from stale data if upstreams haven't replied within this many ms.

stale_max_age.description: How long expired entries are kept for serve-stale, seconds.

groups.description:
Groups it belongs to, highest priority first.
Empty (the default): the group of the device's network (`[[group]] networks`), else
`default` (ADR-050).

match.description:
How to recognize it: an IP (`192.168.1.20`), a CIDR (`10.0.5.0/24`), a MAC
(`aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff`), or a client ID from DoH/DoT (`id:kids-tablet`).

name.description: Device name, shown everywhere and usable in `$client=` rules.

infrastructure.description:
Addresses that are infrastructure, not devices: Kubernetes node and pod networks, a
Docker bridge, a forwarding router. When > 90% of queries come from ≤ 3 of them, the
UI warns that client IPs appear masked (OPS-003). Loopback, this host's default
gateways, and `TELLTALE_NODE_IPS` (set by the Helm chart) are always included.

items.description: IP network, e.g. "192.168.0.0/16" or "fd00::/8" (a bare address means a single host).

neighbor_refresh_secs.description: How often the neighbor table is re-read.

neighbor_table.description:
Read the kernel neighbor table (ARP/NDP) to recognize clients by MAC. Needs host
networking to see real devices (inside a bridge network only the gateway shows up).

trust_edns_mac_from.description:
Forwarders whose EDNS MAC option (dnsmasq `add-mac`) is trusted. Empty = ignore the
option: any client could send it and claim another device's identity.

items.description: IP network, e.g. "192.168.0.0/16" or "fd00::/8" (a bare address means a single host).

bootstrap_secret_file.description:
A shared join secret, in a file (e.g. a Kubernetes Secret). A node holding the cluster
key accepts it like a join token that never expires; a node with `join_url` joins with
it on first start.

config_source.description:
How this node's own configuration is managed (ADR-048): `file` (edited on the node or
in its UI) or `gitops` (rendered from Git, e.g. by the Helm chart under Argo CD). In a
cluster whose config authority is `gitops`, only `gitops` nodes may become primary.

eligible.description: Whether this node may become the cluster primary.

ephemeral.description:
Join as an ephemeral member (CLU-009): never primary, never a voter, dropped from the
registry `ephemeral_ttl_secs` after it was last heard from, shown grouped by site.
An ephemeral node reports ready only once it has the cluster's configuration.

ephemeral_ttl_secs.description: How long the primary keeps an ephemeral member it no longer hears from.

git.description:
Take the cluster's shared configuration from a Git repository (ADR-049): the primary
fetches it, validates it, and publishes it to every node. Set it on every node that
may become primary.

init.description:
Create a cluster on first start when this node isn't in one (CLU-009; the Helm chart's
controller). Same as `telltale cluster init`.

join_url.description:
On first start, join the cluster at this URL with `bootstrap_secret_file` (resolver
pods). The node checks the primary proves it knows the secret before trusting its CA.

listen.description:
The cluster port (mTLS, node-to-node; REQ: CLU-001). Opened only once this node has
joined or created a cluster (`telltale cluster init|join`). Peers dial the URLs given
with `--advertise`, so map this port to those.

site.description: Site label used to group nodes in the UI (e.g. `home-pi`, `k8s`).

ClusterInitConfig.description: `[cluster.init]`: create a cluster on first start.

advertise.description: URLs other nodes reach this node's cluster port at.

negative_trust_anchors.description:
Domains not validated (negative trust anchors, RFC 7646), e.g. an internal domain
forwarded to a server that isn't signed. Routes with `dnssec_nta = true` add theirs.

oneOf.description:
Answers pass through as the upstream sent them (its AD bit is kept for clients that
ask).

Validate every forwarded answer against the root trust anchor: bogus answers become
SERVFAIL with EDE 6, and AD is set only on answers proven here.
Validate and count, but serve bogus answers anyway (for trying validation out).

compile_memory.description: Memory for sorting list entries before spilling to disk (`spec/05` §3.4).

compile_threads.description:
Threads for compiling lists (at low CPU priority). 0 = auto: half the cores, between
1 and 4 (2 on a Pi 4, which compiles 2M names in about 6 s).

fetch_concurrency.description: Lists downloaded at the same time.

fetch_retries.description: Extra attempts after a failed download (network errors, HTTP 5xx, 429).

fetch_timeout_secs.description: Time limit for one download attempt, including the body.

max_list_bytes.description: Downloads larger than this fail and the previous copy is kept.

refresh_secs.description: How often URL and file lists are refreshed (default 24 h, minimum 15 min).

FilterList.description: A filter list (`spec/05` §1). Exactly one source: `url`, `path`, or `rules`.

anyOf.description: Byte count: an integer, or a string with a unit such as "32MiB".

name.description:
Stable ID: lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`, at most 64 characters. Used in file
names, metrics, and the API, so renaming a list re-downloads it.

path.description: Local file, re-read on every refresh.

rules.description: Inline rules, one per entry, in any supported syntax.

GitSourceConfig.description: `[cluster.git]`: the cluster's configuration from a file in a Git repository (ADR-049).

allow_rewind.description: Accept a commit that doesn't descend from the one in use (a force-push or rewind).

credentials_file.description: A file with an access token (or `user:password`) for private repositories.

path.description: The TelltaleDNS file with the shared settings, e.g. `telltale/shared.toml`.

poll_secs.description: How often to check the ref, in seconds.

require_signed.description: Accept only commits SSH-signed by a key in `allowed_signers_file`.

webhook_secret_file.description:
A file with the secret for `POST /api/v1/hooks/git` (GitHub's `X-Hub-Signature-256`),
which checks the ref at once instead of at the next poll.

block_ips.description: Addresses for `block_mode = "custom_ip"` (IPv4 for A, IPv6 for AAAA).

block_ttl.description: TTL of block answers (and of the SOA that lets clients cache a negative block).

color.description: Color for this group in charts and chips (`#rrggbb`); one is picked when unset.

ede.description:
Extended DNS Error on block answers: `blocked` (15) or `filtered` (17, RFC 8914: at
the client's request, e.g. parental controls).

ede_text.description: Include which list blocked the name in the EDE text.

lists.description: Lists (by name) this group uses. Omitted = every enabled list.

name.description: Unique name; `default` applies to clients that match nothing else.

networks.description:
Networks whose devices belong to this group (ADR-050), as IPs or CIDRs, e.g.
`["192.168.2.0/24"]` for a VLAN of smart-home devices. A device gets the group of the most specific
matching network; a `[[client]]` entry with its own `groups` still wins.

items.description: IP network, e.g. "192.168.0.0/16" or "fd00::/8" (a bare address means a single host).

priority.description:
When a client is in several groups, the union of their lists applies and other
settings come from the highest-priority group.

oneOf.description: Try HTTP/3 via Alt-Svc and fall back to HTTP/2.

ListKind.description: Whether a list's rules block or allow (`spec/05` §1). Exception rules (@@) allow regardless.

oneOf.description: The domain and every name below it (Technitium semantics).

path.description: URL path for DoH (default `/dns-query`; `/dns-query/{client-id}` also matches).

proxy_protocol.description: Accept PROXY protocol v2 (TCP-based listeners only).

tls.description: Certificate and key (required for dot/doh/doh3/doq; reloaded on change).

auto_ptr.description: Generate PTR records for every local A/AAAA record.

default_ttl.description: TTL for local records without their own.

hosts_files.description: Hosts files (`IP name [alias...]` per line) to import as A/AAAA records.

name.description: Owner name; a leading `*.` makes it a wildcard for names below it.

node_only.description:
Keep this record on this node only (CLU-006): a cluster primary doesn't share it, and
a replica keeps it next to the cluster's records.

per_client_cap.description: At most this many clients get their own series (default 100); the rest are "other".

data_dir.description: The only writable directory (snapshots, state.db, query log).

drain_delay_secs.description:
REQ: OPS-007 — on shutdown, keep answering this many seconds after reporting not ready,
so load balancers and Kubernetes Services stop sending queries first (the Helm charts
set 5). 0 stops as soon as in-flight lookups finish. At most 60.

name.description: Node name; empty means the hostname.

workers.description: UDP worker threads; 0 means `min(cgroup CPU limit, cores)`.

OidcConfig.description:
`OpenID Connect` sign-in (API-004, `spec/08` §6, ADR-034). Each provider gets a "Sign in
with ..." button; users are created on first sign-in and their role comes from a claim
(groups) at every sign-in. Changes need a restart.

allowed_admin_networks.description: Where break-glass admin sign-in is allowed. Default: private networks and loopback.

items.description: IP network, e.g. "192.168.0.0/16" or "fd00::/8" (a bare address means a single host).

disable_local_login.description:
Turn off password sign-in (and HTTP Basic) except for admins signing in from
`allowed_admin_networks` (break-glass, for when the provider is down).

public_url.description:
Where people open the UI, e.g. `https://dns.example.com` or `http://192.168.1.2:8053`.
Each provider's redirect URI is `<public_url>/api/v1/auth/oidc/<id>/callback`, and
after sign-out the provider returns to `<public_url>/`; register both with it.

client_secret_file.description: ... a file holding it (a mounted Kubernetes Secret). Neither: a public client (PKCE).

default_role.description: Role for users whose groups match no rule. Unset: they can't sign in.

groups_claim.description:
Claim listing the user's groups or roles (`groups`, `roles`,
`realm_access.roles`). Default `groups`.

id.description: Short ID used in URLs: lowercase letters, digits, and `-` (`keycloak`, `authentik`).

name.description: Button label ("Sign in with ..."). Default: the ID.

require_verified_email.description: Refuse users whose provider says their email isn't verified.

role.description: Group → role rules; a user gets the highest role any of their groups maps to.

username_claim.description:
Claim that becomes the TelltaleDNS username (dotted paths reach into objects).
Default `preferred_username`; falls back to `email`, then `sub`.

flush_interval_secs.description: Flush the in-progress block after this many seconds.

privacy_level.description: 0 full; 1 hide domains; 2 hide domains + clients; 3 aggregates only.

retention_bytes.description: Delete oldest segments beyond this total size.

retention_days.description: Delete segments older than this many days.

RateLimitAction.description: What to do with a rate-limited query.

items.description: IP network, e.g. "192.168.0.0/16" or "fd00::/8" (a bare address means a single host).

ipv4_prefix.description: Count IPv4 clients per /N (32 = per address).

ipv6_prefix.description: Count IPv6 clients per /N (64 groups a device's rotating privacy addresses).

queries.description: Queries allowed per `window_secs` per client (token bucket; bursts up to this).

oneOf.description: Resolver + controller in one process (Pi / single node).

dnssec_nta.description: Add a DNSSEC negative trust anchor for the suffixes (local zones are usually unsigned).

match_group.description: Client group names this route applies to (empty = all).

match_qtype.description: Query types this route applies to, e.g. `["PTR"]` (empty = all).

RuleConfig.description:
REQ: FLT-005, FLT-006 (T6.12, ADR-067) — a quick rule: allow or block a domain and its
subdomains for chosen devices, groups, or everyone, optionally until a time.

created.description: When it was made (RFC 3339), filled in by the API.

created_by.description: Who made it (a user or `agent:<token>`), filled in by the API.

devices.description: Devices it applies to: device names (`[[client]] name`), IPs, or CIDRs.

domain.description: The domain; its subdomains are included (`example.com` covers `www.example.com`).

expires.description: When it stops applying (RFC 3339, e.g. `2026-10-05T21:30:00Z`). Absent: never.

groups.description: Groups it applies to. With neither `devices` nor `groups`, it applies to everyone.

id.description: A unique ID (the API assigns one; in a file, any unique name).

note.description: Why it exists ("Mom's game"), shown with every decision it makes.

buffer_bytes.description:
Most query log kept here while it can't be delivered; the oldest goes first beyond it.
Put `[node] data_dir` on tmpfs (or accept the writes) on an SD card.

interval_secs.description:
Close and ship the query log at least this often, in seconds (it's searchable from
this node until then, through the cluster).

to.description: The node that stores this node's query log: a node ID or site. Default: the primary.

SpecialConfig.description: Built-in handling of special names (`spec/03` §3 step 4).

block_firefox_canary.description: `use-application-dns.net` → NXDOMAIN, so Firefox doesn't switch to its own DoH.

private_ptr_nxdomain.description:
Reverse lookups for private addresses → NXDOMAIN instead of asking public upstreams,
unless a local record or route covers them (Pi-hole "bogus-priv").

anomaly.description: Per-device anomaly detection (OBS-013): alert-only, deterministic, explainable.

ring_slots.description:
Event ring size per producing thread, in events of ~128 bytes (power of two, at
least 1024). The default, 4096 (512 KiB), holds about 170 ms of a fully loaded
worker; a full ring drops events (counted), never queries (ADR-026).

TelemetryMode.description: Where detailed query events go (`spec/12` CLU-007).

oneOf.description: Keep the query log on this node.

Ship the query log to another cluster node (the primary by default), keeping only a
small local buffer until it's delivered (store-and-forward, CLU-007): for nodes with
little or wear-sensitive storage, such as a Pi on an SD card, and ephemeral pods.

check.description:
Read this build's channel's signed release index once a day to see whether a newer
build exists. `false`: nothing leaves the node, and the status is `off`.

index_url.description:
Where to read the index instead of GitHub (a mirror); its signature is still checked
with the release key built into the binary.

bootstrap.description:
DNS servers used to resolve a hostname URL (UPS-009); default: the system resolvers
from /etc/resolv.conf, minus our own listeners. To pin the server address instead, put
the IP in the URL and set `tls_server_name`.

ecs.description: ECS handling: `strip` (default), `pass`, or a CIDR to substitute (P1).

headers.description: Extra HTTP headers for DoH (e.g. an auth token).

name.description: Unique name referenced by upstream groups.

tls_insecure_skip_verify.description: Disable certificate verification (dangerous; logs a warning).

members.description: Upstream names, in priority order for `failover`.

name.description: Unique group name. Queries that match no route use the group named `default`.

parallel_fanout.description: How many members to race (strategy `parallel` only).

oneOf.description: Viewer, plus pause, cache flush, and managing lists, clients, and groups.
